transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. I'm here because... well, I'm a barber, and I've gotten to the point where I'll do pretty much anything to avoid using a straight razor at work. I'll switch clients with my coworkers, or tell the customer the blade is missing, or just hide it in a drawer. And if I absolutely can't get out of doing a hot towel shave... I'm just shaking through the whole thing. It's getting really bad.
When you think about or see other sharp objects—like needles, knives, or scissors—do you feel the same kind of fear and avoidance that you do with the straight razor?

No, it's really just the straight razor. I mean, I use scissors all day long at work and it doesn't bother me at all. Needles don't really bother me either, and I'm fine using knives when I cook at home. It's... it's specifically that straight razor.
When you think about using the straight razor, what exactly are you afraid will happen? Are you worried about cutting yourself or seeing blood, or is it something else about the razor itself?

It's... well, I know it’s just a tool. I mean, it's something I trained with, and I can use clippers all day long without a second thought. But when that straight razor is just sitting open at my station, it feels like I’m about to hurt somebody, or cut myself really badly. That's what I'm afraid of. I just get this intense feeling that a severe cut is going to happen.

When you have that feeling that you're about to hurt somebody with the razor, do these thoughts just pop into your head on their own, even when you're trying not to think about them? Or is it more that the razor itself makes you anxious?

No, they don't really just pop into my head out of nowhere. Like, if I'm driving home or just hanging out, I'm not thinking about it at all. It's... it's really just the razor itself. When I see it sitting there on my station, or when I know I have to pick it up for a shave, that's when all that fear hits me. So yeah, it's definitely the physical razor that makes me anxious, not just random thoughts.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F42.4 (OCD). Patient denies intrusive thoughts occurring outside of the presence of the trigger (straight razor). The fear is situational and tied to the specific object, not driven by obsessive thoughts. This is consistent with specific phobia (F40.1) rather than OCD, which typically involves unwanted intrusive thoughts that persist even when the trigger is absent.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a specific phobia of straight razors, meeting criteria for F40.1 (Social phobia). The fear is circumscribed to a particular object (straight razor), triggered by exposure to or anticipation of that object, and accompanied by avoidance behaviors and anxiety symptoms (shaking). The fear is not part of intrusive thoughts or obsessions, but rather a conditioned anxiety response to a specific stimulus. While F42.4 (OCD with predominantly obsessional thoughts) was considered due to the mention of intrusive-seeming fear about cutting, the patient clarified that these thoughts are not ego-dystonic intrusions but rather rational anxiety responses to the feared object itself, making specific phobia the more accurate diagnosis.
